title: Ekaślokī
subtitle: A dialogue on the light of awareness

source.edition: The Works of Sri Sankaracharya, vol. 16, Sri Vani Vilas Press, 1910
source.digitalText: Ambuda CC0 1.0; machine-readable text credit: Arun Prasad

units.label: Verse 1
units.deva:
किं ज्योतिस्तव भानुमानहनि मे रात्रौ प्रदीपादिकं
स्यादेवं रविदीपदर्शनविधौ किं ज्योतिराख्याहि मे ।
चक्षुस्तस्य निमीलनादिसमये किं धीर्धियो दर्शने
किं तत्राहमतो भवान्परमकं ज्योतिस्तदस्मि प्रभो ॥
units.translation: “What is your light?” “The sun by day; at night, a lamp and the like.” “When the sun and lamp are being perceived, what is the light? Tell me.” “The eye.” “When the eye is closed, what?” “The mind.” “When the mind is known, what is the light there?” “I am.” Therefore, O Lord, you are the supreme light; I am that.

gloss.en: at the time of closing [the eyes] and so forth

units.label: Colophon
units.deva: इति श्रीमत्परमहंसपरिव्राजकाचार्यस्य श्रीगोविन्दभगवत्पूज्यपादशिष्यस्य श्रीमच्छङ्करभगवतः कृतौ एकश्लोकी संपूर्णा ॥
units.translation: Thus ends the Ekaślokī, composed by the revered Śaṅkara, disciple of the revered Govinda Bhagavatpāda, the eminent teacher and wandering paramahaṃsa.

gloss.en: of the teacher of wandering renunciants
